claim_summary: FETA contributes a fixed multi-agent time-series classification workflow combining channel selection, DTW exemplar retrieval, prompted per-channel reasoning, and confidence-weighted decision aggregation.

claim_evidence.quote: FETA, a multi-agent framework for trainingfree TSC via exemplar-based in-context reasoning. FETA decomposes a multivariate series into channel-wise subproblems, retrieves a few structurally similar labeled examples for each channel

modules.name: Task-driven channel selection
modules.scope_reason: R3_1 applies because channel ranking optimizes class separation and nearest-neighbor classification; changing task family changes the selection objective. Its channel-wise temporal preprocessing is embedded in this classifier, so it is not a task-independent GTS module.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - relevance score uses class separation and classification accuracy

evidence.quote: Channels are then ranked by Sc, and the top-M are selected for downstream reasoning.

modules.name: DTW exemplar retrieval
modules.scope_reason: R3_1 applies because retrieval selects labeled examples to support classification; another task family would require a different retrieval objective and label use. DTW alignment and retrieving time-series precedents are temporal operations within this task procedure, not an independent task-agnostic GTS module.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - retrieves labeled neighbors for classification

evidence.quote: For each selected channel c ∈ S and a test sequence X∗(c), the Example Retriever searches for its Kr most similar training sequences using Dynamic Time Warping (DTW)

modules.name: Exemplar-grounded channel reasoning
modules.scope_reason: R2 places the prompt and in-context procedure in the Harness because model parameters are unchanged. R3_1 applies because the reasoner adjudicates class labels for this classification task; changing tasks changes its required output and prompt. It does not provide task-independent temporal processing as a separate GTS module.
rubric_path: R2:Harness - prompt/in-context procedure, no parameter updates
R3_1_TSK:yes - outputs a channel-level class decision

evidence.quote: The Channel Reasoner therefore leverages a reasoning LLM to perform in-context comparison of temporal patterns

modules.name: Confidence-weighted class aggregation
modules.scope_reason: R3_1 applies because the aggregator combines class labels and confidence values to produce the classification output; a different task requires a different output space and aggregation rule. It does not meet GTS because the mechanism is task-objective-specific rather than generally managing temporal state.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - fuses class predictions into the final classification

evidence.quote: The final stage aggregates channel-level predictions into a single decision. Because different channels may provide complementary or conflicting evidence, the aggregator combines labels {ŷc}c∈S and confidences {wc}c∈S into a robust consensus via confidence-weighted fusion.

task_performance.quote: We adopt the official train/test splits and report classification accuracy.

notes: The paper reports classification accuracy and ablations, but not runtime execution validity, temporal leakage or information-availability checks, or downstream decision utility.
